rationale: Lattice refinement skips the cells near the zero level set whose sampled minimum is > 0 (only cells that already straddle a failure are refined), so a failure hidden between the base lattice points is never found (R4-3 corrected).
The Lipschitz safety factor 2 is dropped in the lattice certificate: the cell bound uses the bare measured local slopes (R4-3 corrected: L = 2 x the measured local slopes).
Breakpoint bracketing takes the BETTER of the two one-sided linearizations instead of the worse, so a bracketed point can hide the failing side (R4-7: the requirement must hold for both).

Bracketing is applied to trim failures (INFEASIBLE, or NOT_CONVERGED at stage trim): a physical failure near a breakpoint is turned into an OK point by its neighbours (R4-7: physical failures are never bracketed).

The staged run re-runs only groups whose CSR bracket lies INSIDE [0.8, 1.2] instead of every bracket that OVERLAPS it, so a wide bracket straddling the band (e.g. [0, 2.76]) is never re-run at the full budget (R4-8).
Lateral groups drop Cm_q without the gate: a failed invariance check does not restore the full set of parameters (R4-9: gated, with a fallback).

The lattice re-evaluates points it has already evaluated (no evaluation store), so the shared lattice is not evaluated once per candidate condition (R4-3 corrected: one evaluation pass reused by every group, shape and alpha).
Stage 2 of the staged run re-runs the selected groups at the stage-1 (reduced) budget instead of the full budget, so it can never resolve what stage 1 could not (R4-8).

The lattice's equal-percentage shape is built from the judged half-widths instead of 10 % for every parameter, so the 'equal' CSR of the longitudinal groups re-imports the judged ratios (R4-1(b) on the R4b lattice path).
